facts.raw_span: A man in his 80s was brought to the emergency department after a cardiac arrest
the patient was last seen healthy by his family 4 hours earlier
then was found unresponsive and pulseless in the bathroom
He underwent cardiopulmonary resuscitation, receiving 4 doses of epinephrine intravenously and endotracheal tube intubation with return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 10 minutes
Family later revealed he had chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and had been complaining of shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation
A family member witnessed him struggling for air before losing consciousness
Initial rhythm was pulseless electrical activity
Sinus rhythm at approximately 100 beats per minute
Right axis deviation
Prolonged QRS duration with rsR' complexes in lead V1
No acute occlusions found
QT interval of 360 ms measurable in leads V4-V6

concepts.why: The patient's initial rhythm was pulseless electrical activity and had a prolonged QRS duration with rsR' complexes in lead V1, suggesting acute coronary syndrome.
The patient had a history of COPD and was complaining of shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation, indicating a COPD exacerbation.
The patient's ECG showed right axis deviation and a prolonged QT interval, which can be indicative of hypokalemia.
The patient's ECG showed a prolonged QRS duration with rsR' complexes in lead V1, which can be indicative of hyperkalemia.
The patient's initial rhythm was pulseless electrical activity and had a sinus rhythm at approximately 100 beats per minute, suggesting a cardiac arrhythmia.
The patient had a history of COPD and was complaining of shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation, which could be indicative of a pulmonary embolism.
The patient's ECG showed right axis deviation and a prolonged QT interval, which can be indicative of an electrolyte imbalance.
The patient's initial rhythm was pulseless electrical activity and had a prolonged QRS duration with rsR' complexes in lead V1, which can be indicative of cardiomyopathy.

rationales.F01: Cardiac arrest suggests cardiac arrhythmia or other cardiac conditions.
rationales.F05: COPD and shortness of breath suggest a COPD exacerbation.
rationales.F06: Struggling for air before losing consciousness suggests a respiratory issue like COPD exacerbation.
rationales.F07: Pulseless electrical activity is not typical of acute coronary syndrome.
rationales.F10: Prolonged QRS duration can be associated with hyperkalemia or cardiac arrhythmia.
rationales.F11: No acute occlusions found makes acute coronary syndrome less likely.
